Challenging the Award passed by the Tribunal, the 4th respondent/Insurance Company preferred this Civil Miscellaneous Appeal.

2.The learned counsel for the appellants would argue on various grounds that the Tribunal went wrong in holding that the alleged accident was caused by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Tractor Trailer bearing Reg.No.TN 15 Z 6561 and went wrong in awarding a compensation of Rs.7,86,380/-.

Further, the appellant being the insurer of the Trailer and the 3rd https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on: 10/07/2025 11:33:07 am ) respondent being the insurer of the tractor are equally liable to pay the compensation to the claimants.

He would submit that the Tribunal failed to appreciate that the accident occurred due to the negligence of the deceased who drove the motor cycle bearing Reg. No. TN 32 AY 2234 in a rash and negligent manner and hit on the tractor trailer and went wrong in holding that the driver of the Tractor Trailer is responsible for the accident.

The Tribunal failed to appreciate that the owner -cum- driver of the Tractor Trailer was examined as RW2 and he clearly deposed that at the time of accident, he parked the Tractor Trailer on the side of the mud road, at that time, the rider of the motor cycle ride the same in a rash and negligent manner by carrying three pillion riders and hit on the Tractor Trailer and resulting in the accident.

The Tribunal failed to appreciate that the deceased who drove the motor cycle in a rash and negligent manner by carrying more than the permitted persons, without wearing helmet, hit on the Tractor Trailer and went wrong in holding that the driver of the Tractor Trailer is responsible for the accident and the alleged accident was caused by the negligence of the driver of the Tractor Trailer without any basis whatsoever.
The assessment and award of the Tribunal is against the principles laid down by the Apex Court.

3.The learned counsel for the 3rd respondent would submit that the Tribunal ought not to have granted award since there is a gross violation of the https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on: 10/07/2025 11:33:07 am ) policy conditions on the side of the deceased.
Furthermore, the contributory negligence fixed by the Tribunal is also very less in nature.
Therefore, he prayed to set aside the findings of the Tribunal.
4.The learned counsel for the respondents/claimants would argue that based on the Award passed by the Tribunal, the 3rd respondent/Insurance Company has already deposited the award amount.
The Insurance Company alone challenged the Award passed by the Tribunal.
However, the Tribunal has fixed the contributory negligence on the side of the deceased, while granting the Award is well reasoned one and needs no interference.

5.Considering the submissions made on either side, the fact reveals that four persons have travelled in a two wheeler and according to the claimants, the driver of the Tractor Trailer belongs to the 1st Royal Sundaram General Insurance ... vs Vijaya on 9 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/180766547/
4 respondent, suddenly turned on the road side, thereby, the rider of the two wheeler was not able to control the vehicle and hit against the Tractor Trailer, therefore, the accident was occurred.

sentences.text: Due to the road accident, all the four persons died.
Out of which, one person was married and other three persons were unmarried.
Their legal heirs have filed all the Claim Petitions before the Tribunal.
At the time of accident, the rider of the two wheeler had three pillion riders.

It also reveals that the https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on: 10/07/2025 11:33:07 am ) deceased Elumalai rode the two wheeler with three pillion riders and without wearing helmet and there is a violation of policy conditions.

The claimants are able to establish that due to the negligent driving of the driver of the Tractor Trailer, the accident was happened, but however, there is an oral evidence on the side of the respondents, challenging the manner of the accident.

As per the eye witness, the claimants are able to establish that the accident was occurred due to the negligent driving of the driver of the Tractor Trailer, but however, on the side of the deceased also, there is a gross violation of policy conditions.
6.While awarding compensation, the Tribunal fixed the contributory negligence of 30% on the side of the rider of the two wheeler and 20% was fixed on the side of each pillion riders.
Furthermore, the accident is of the year 2014 and the monthly income was fixed at Rs.8,000/-.
Considering the Post- mortem Certificate of the deceased, the age has been fixed and the Tribunal has rightly fixed the contributory negligence on the side of the deceased.
Therefore, the objections raised by the learned counsel for the appellant is unsustainable one.
Accordingly, all the Civil Miscellaneous Appeals are dismissed as no merits and the findings rendered by the Tribunal are confirmed.
